rounds.text: Interiors & More Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 349 per share compared to a market price of ₹ 180, providing a substantial margin of safety of 48.5% [E32, E33]. The business demonstrates exceptional operating momentum, highlighted by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 64% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 110% [E8, E11], alongside robust trailing twelve-month sales growth of 47% [E10] and net profit growth exceeding 50% YoY [E51]. This fundamental outperformance is further supported by a high-performing Consumer Durables sector tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.72, where the company easily outpaces the sector median ROCE of 9.9% with its own healthy ROCE of 16.0% [E6, E57, E60]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only prices in a modest 8.9% earnings growth, whereas the base case assumes 18.0%, suggesting the market is overly pessimistic despite results scoring 90 out of 100 on recent improvement [E34, E56]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed to 24% from 38% three years prior [E18], and free cash flow sits at Rs -22 Cr due to heavy capital expenditure build-up seen in capital work-in-progress rising by 328.6% to Rs 30 Cr [E24, E28].

Interiors & More Ltd carries severe structural and quality-of-earnings risks that undermine its headline growth numbers. Operating margins have collapsed by 14 percentage points to 24% in March 2026 compared to three years earlier, and the data provider explicitly flags a critical accounting warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E18, E47]. Cash generation is deeply disconnected from reported profits, evidenced by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.50x, an operating cash flow of only 51% of operating profit, and a sprawling negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 [E22, E24, E25]. This cash burn has driven borrowings up sharply to Rs 56 Cr from Rs 29 Cr a year earlier, alongside a massive 328.6% surge in Capital Work-in-Progress to Rs 30 Cr [E27, E28]. Institutional conviction is clearly eroding as foreign institutional holdings dropped from 8.58% in March 2024 to 4.40% in March 2026, while the stock languishes with a weak relative-strength rating of 22 and sits near the bottom of its 52-week range [E30, E38, E35]. conceded: [E8], [E11], [E32], [E33]

While the bear highlights a margin compression to 24% [E18], it overlooks that sales growth remains phenomenal at 47% TTM and 64% over five years, vastly outperforming the sector median sales growth of 11.0% [E8, E10, E59]. The concern over rising borrowings to Rs 56 Cr and negative free cash flow [E24, E27] is a byproduct of heavy investment in future capacity, specifically a 328.6% surge in Capital Work-in-Progress to Rs 30 Cr [E28], aligning with a consumer durables sector tailwind score of +0.72 [E57]. The market price of ₹ 180 leaves an exceptional 48.5% margin of safety relative to a DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 349 [E32, E33], and the reverse DCF indicates the current price only prices in a modest 8.9% growth rate against the base case of 18.0% [E34]. Furthermore, profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 44% [E44], signaling a classic disconnect where improving fundamentals are obscured by short-term sentiment. Conceded: [E22], [E47].

The bull points to phenomenal sales growth [E8, E10], but ignores that this expansion has come at the severe expense of profitability, with operating margins collapsing by 14 percentage points to 24% and an inconsistent margin trend [E18, E20]. While the bull dismisses negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr [E24] and rising borrowings of Rs 56 Cr [E27] as mere growth investments, the data provider explicitly flags a critical accounting risk that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E47]. The claimed margin of safety [E33] and undervaluation [E32] offer little comfort when paired with a severe cash conversion ratio of just 0.50x, signalling that reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual cash generation [E22]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have dumped their holdings from 8.58% down to 4.40% [E30], and the stock suffers from a dismal relative strength rating of 22 alongside a catastrophic 52-week price collapse of 66.3% [E38, E39]. Conceded: [E8], [E10], [E34].
